20 /-!
21 # Basic definitions about sets
22 
23 In this file we define various operations on sets.
24 We also provide basic lemmas needed to unfold the definitions.
25 More advanced theorems about these definitions are located in other files in `Mathlib/Data/Set`.
26 
27 ## Main definitions
28 
29 - complement of a set and set difference;
30 - `Set.preimage f s`, a.k.a. `f ⁻¹' s`: preimage of a set;
31 - `Set.range f`: the range of a function;
32   it is more general than `f '' univ` because it allows functions from `Sort*`;
33 - `s ×ˢ t`: product of `s : Set α` and `t : Set β` as a set in `α × β`;
34 - `Set.diagonal`: the diagonal in `α × α`;
35 - `Set.offDiag s`: the part of `s ×ˢ s` that is off the diagonal;
36 - `Set.pi`: indexed product of a family of sets `∀ i, Set (α i)`,
37   as a set in `∀ i, α i`;
38 - `Set.EqOn f g s`: the predicate saying that two functions are equal on a set;
39 - `Set.MapsTo f s t`: the predicate saying that `f` sends all points of `s` to `t`;
40 - `Set.MapsTo.restrict`: restrict `f : α → β` to `f' : s → t` provided that `Set.MapsTo f s t`;
41 - `Set.restrictPreimage`: restrict `f : α → β` to `f' : (f ⁻¹' t) → t`;
42 - `Set.InjOn`: the predicate saying that `f` is injective on a set;
43 - `Set.SurjOn f s t`: the predicate saying that `t ⊆ f '' s`;
44 - `Set.BijOn f s t`: the predicate saying that `f` is injective on `s` and `f '' s = t`;
45 - `Set.graphOn`: the graph of a function on a set;
46 - `Set.LeftInvOn`, `Set.RightInvOn`, `Set.InvOn`:
47   the predicates saying that `f'` is a left, right or two-sided inverse of `f` on `s`, `t`, or both;
48 - `Set.image2`: the image of a pair of sets under a binary operation,
49   mostly useful to define pointwise algebraic operations on sets;
50 - `Set.seq`: monadic `seq` operation on sets;
51   we don't use monadic notation to ensure support for maps between different universes.
52 
53 ## Notation
54 
55 - `f '' s`: image of a set;
56 - `f ⁻¹' s`: preimage of a set;
57 - `s ×ˢ t`: the product of sets;
58 - `s ∪ t`: the union of two sets;
59 - `s ∩ t`: the intersection of two sets;
60 - `sᶜ`: the complement of a set;
61 - `s \ t`: the difference of two sets.
62 
63 ## Keywords
64 
65 set, image, preimage
66 -/
67

71 
72 namespace Set
73 
74 variable {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {γ : Type w}

76 /-! ### Lemmas about `mem` and `setOf` -/
77 
78 @[simp, mfld_simps, push]
79 theorem mem_setOf_eq {x : α} {p : α → Prop} : (x ∈ {y | p y}) = p x := rfl
80 
81 grind_pattern mem_setOf_eq => x ∈ setOf p
82 
83 /-- This lemma is intended for use with `rw` where a membership predicate is needed,
84 hence the explicit argument and the equality in the reverse direction from normal.
85 See also `Set.mem_setOf_eq` for the reverse direction applied to an argument. -/
86 theorem eq_mem_setOf (p : α → Prop) : p = (· ∈ {a | p a}) := rfl
87 
88 theorem mem_setOf {a : α} {p : α → Prop} : a ∈ { x | p x } ↔ p a := Iff.rfl
89 
90 /-- If `h : a ∈ {x | p x}` then `h.out : p x`. These are definitionally equal, but this can
91 nevertheless be useful for various reasons, e.g. to apply further projection notation or in an
92 argument to `simp`. -/
93 alias ⟨_root_.Membership.mem.out, _⟩ := mem_setOf
94 
95 theorem notMem_setOf_iff {a : α} {p : α → Prop} : a ∉ { x | p x } ↔ ¬p a := Iff.rfl
96 
97 @[simp] theorem setOf_mem_eq {s : Set α} : { x | x ∈ s } = s := rfl
98 
99 @[simp, mfld_simps, grind ←, push]
100 theorem mem_univ (x : α) : x ∈ @univ α := trivial
101 
102 /-! ### Operations -/
103 
104 instance : Compl (Set α) := ⟨fun s ↦ {x | x ∉ s}⟩
105 
106 @[simp, grind =, push]
107 theorem mem_compl_iff (s : Set α) (x : α) : x ∈ sᶜ ↔ x ∉ s := Iff.rfl
108 
109 theorem diff_eq (s t : Set α) : s \ t = s ∩ tᶜ := rfl
110 
111 @[simp, grind =, push]
112 theorem mem_diff {s t : Set α} (x : α) : x ∈ s \ t ↔ x ∈ s ∧ x ∉ t := Iff.rfl
113 
114 theorem mem_diff_of_mem {s t : Set α} {x : α} (h1 : x ∈ s) (h2 : x ∉ t) : x ∈ s \ t := ⟨h1, h2⟩
115 
116 /-- The preimage of `s : Set β` by `f : α → β`, written `f ⁻¹' s`,
117   is the set of `x : α` such that `f x ∈ s`. -/
118 def preimage (f : α → β) (s : Set β) : Set α := {x | f x ∈ s}
119 
120 /-- `f ⁻¹' t` denotes the preimage of `t : Set β` under the function `f : α → β`. -/
121 infixl:80 " ⁻¹' " => preimage
122 
123 @[simp, mfld_simps, grind =, push]
124 theorem mem_preimage {f : α → β} {s : Set β} {a : α} : a ∈ f ⁻¹' s ↔ f a ∈ s := Iff.rfl
125 
126 /-- `f '' s` denotes the image of `s : Set α` under the function `f : α → β`. -/
127 infixl:80 " '' " => image
128 
129 @[simp, grind =, push]
130 theorem mem_image (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (y : β) : y ∈ f '' s ↔ ∃ x ∈ s, f x = y :=
131   Iff.rfl
132 
133 @[mfld_simps]
134 theorem mem_image_of_mem (f : α → β) {x : α} {a : Set α} (h : x ∈ a) : f x ∈ f '' a :=
135   ⟨_, h, rfl⟩
136 
137 /-- Restriction of `f` to `s` factors through `s.imageFactorization f : s → f '' s`. -/
138 def imageFactorization (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : s → f '' s := fun p =>
139   ⟨f p.1, mem_image_of_mem f p.2⟩
140 
141 /-- `kernImage f s` is the set of `y` such that `f ⁻¹ y ⊆ s`. -/
142 def kernImage (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Set β := {y | ∀ ⦃x⦄, f x = y → x ∈ s}
143 
144 lemma subset_kernImage_iff {s : Set β} {t : Set α} {f : α → β} : s ⊆ kernImage f t ↔ f ⁻¹' s ⊆ t :=
145   ⟨fun h _ hx ↦ h hx rfl,
146     fun h _ hx y hy ↦ h (show f y ∈ s from hy.symm ▸ hx)⟩
147 
148 section Range
149 
150 variable {ι : Sort*} {f : ι → α}
151 
152 /-- Range of a function.
153 
154 This function is more flexible than `f '' univ`, as the image requires that the domain is in Type
155 and not an arbitrary Sort. -/
156 def range (f : ι → α) : Set α := {x | ∃ y, f y = x}
157 
158 @[simp, grind =, push] theorem mem_range {x : α} : x ∈ range f ↔ ∃ y, f y = x := Iff.rfl
159 
160 @[mfld_simps] theorem mem_range_self (i : ι) : f i ∈ range f := ⟨i, rfl⟩
161 
162 /-- Any map `f : ι → α` factors through a map `rangeFactorization f : ι → range f`. -/
163 def rangeFactorization (f : ι → α) : ι → range f := fun i => ⟨f i, mem_range_self i⟩
164 
165 @[simp] lemma rangeFactorization_injective :
166     (Set.rangeFactorization f).Injective ↔ f.Injective := by
167   simp [Function.Injective, rangeFactorization]
168 
169 @[simp] lemma rangeFactorization_surjective : (rangeFactorization f).Surjective :=
170   fun ⟨_, i, rfl⟩ ↦ ⟨i, rfl⟩
171 
172 @[simp] lemma rangeFactorization_bijective :
173     (Set.rangeFactorization f).Bijective ↔ f.Injective := by simp [Function.Bijective]
174 
175 @[simp] lemma rangeFactorization_eq_rangeFactorization_iff {ι : Sort*} {α : Type*} {f : ι → α}
176     (a b : ι) : Set.rangeFactorization f a = Set.rangeFactorization f b ↔ f a = f b := by
177   simp [Set.rangeFactorization]
178 
179 lemma rangeFactorization_eq_iff {ι : Sort*} {α : Type*} {f : ι → α} (a : ι) (b : Set.range f) :
180     Set.rangeFactorization f a = b ↔ f a = b := by
181   rw [Set.rangeFactorization, ← b.coe_eta b.2, Subtype.ext_iff]
182 
183 end Range
184 
185 /-- We can use the axiom of choice to pick a preimage for every element of `range f`. -/
186 noncomputable def rangeSplitting (f : α → β) : range f → α := fun x => x.2.choose
187 
188 -- This cannot be a `@[simp]` lemma because the head of the left-hand side is a variable.
189 theorem apply_rangeSplitting (f : α → β) (x : range f) : f (rangeSplitting f x) = x :=
190   x.2.choose_spec
191 
192 @[simp]
193 theorem comp_rangeSplitting (f : α → β) : f ∘ rangeSplitting f = Subtype.val := by
194   ext
195   simp only [Function.comp_apply]
196   apply apply_rangeSplitting
197 
198 lemma Subtype.range_coind (f : α → β) {p : β → Prop} (h : ∀ (a : α), p (f a)) :
199     range (Subtype.coind f h) = Subtype.val ⁻¹' range f := by
200   simp [Set.ext_iff, Subtype.ext_iff]
201 
202 section Prod
203 
204 /-- The Cartesian product `Set.prod s t` is the set of `(a, b)` such that `a ∈ s` and `b ∈ t`. -/
205 def prod (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Set (α × β) := {p | p.1 ∈ s ∧ p.2 ∈ t}
206 
207 @[default_instance]
208 instance instSProd : SProd (Set α) (Set β) (Set (α × β)) where
209   sprod := Set.prod
210 
211 theorem prod_eq (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : s ×ˢ t = Prod.fst ⁻¹' s ∩ Prod.snd ⁻¹' t := rfl
212 
213 variable {a : α} {b : β} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {p : α × β}
214 
215 theorem mem_prod_eq : (p ∈ s ×ˢ t) = (p.1 ∈ s ∧ p.2 ∈ t) := rfl
216 
217 @[simp, mfld_simps, grind =, push]
218 theorem mem_prod : p ∈ s ×ˢ t ↔ p.1 ∈ s ∧ p.2 ∈ t := .rfl
219 
220 @[mfld_simps, push only high] /- This `push` lemma is so that `(a, b) ∈ s ×ˢ t` gets turned
221 into `a ∈ s ∧ b ∈ t`, instead of getting `(a, b).1` and `(a, b).2`. -/
222 theorem prodMk_mem_set_prod_eq : ((a, b) ∈ s ×ˢ t) = (a ∈ s ∧ b ∈ t) :=
223   rfl
224 
225 theorem mk_mem_prod (ha : a ∈ s) (hb : b ∈ t) : (a, b) ∈ s ×ˢ t := ⟨ha, hb⟩
226 
227 theorem prod_image_left (f : α → γ) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) :
228     (f '' s) ×ˢ t = (fun x ↦ (f x.1, x.2)) '' s ×ˢ t := by
229   aesop
230 
231 theorem prod_image_right (f : α → γ) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) :
232     t ×ˢ (f '' s) = (fun x ↦ (x.1, f x.2)) '' t ×ˢ s := by
233   aesop
234 
235 end Prod
236 
237 section Diagonal
238 
239 /-- `diagonal α` is the set of `α × α` consisting of all pairs of the form `(a, a)`. -/
240 def diagonal (α : Type*) : Set (α × α) := {p | p.1 = p.2}
241 
242 theorem mem_diagonal (x : α) : (x, x) ∈ diagonal α := rfl
243 
244 @[simp, grind =, push] theorem mem_diagonal_iff {x : α × α} : x ∈ diagonal α ↔ x.1 = x.2 := .rfl
245 
246 /-- The off-diagonal of a set `s` is the set of pairs `(a, b)` with `a, b ∈ s` and `a ≠ b`. -/
247 def offDiag (s : Set α) : Set (α × α) := {x | x.1 ∈ s ∧ x.2 ∈ s ∧ x.1 ≠ x.2}
248 
249 @[simp, grind =, push]
250 theorem mem_offDiag {x : α × α} {s : Set α} : x ∈ s.offDiag ↔ x.1 ∈ s ∧ x.2 ∈ s ∧ x.1 ≠ x.2 :=
251   Iff.rfl
252 
253 end Diagonal
254 
255 section Pi
256 
257 variable {ι : Type*} {α : ι → Type*}
258 
259 /-- Given an index set `ι` and a family of sets `t : Π i, Set (α i)`, `pi s t`
260 is the set of dependent functions `f : Πa, π a` such that `f i` belongs to `t i`
261 whenever `i ∈ s`. -/
262 def pi (s : Set ι) (t : ∀ i, Set (α i)) : Set (∀ i, α i) := {f | ∀ i ∈ s, f i ∈ t i}
263 
264 variable {s : Set ι} {t : ∀ i, Set (α i)} {f : ∀ i, α i}
265 
266 @[simp, grind =, push] theorem mem_pi : f ∈ s.pi t ↔ ∀ i ∈ s, f i ∈ t i := .rfl
267 
268 theorem mem_univ_pi : f ∈ pi univ t ↔ ∀ i, f i ∈ t i := by simp
269 
270 end Pi
271 
272 /-- Two functions `f₁ f₂ : α → β` are equal on `s` if `f₁ x = f₂ x` for all `x ∈ s`. -/
273 def EqOn (f₁ f₂ : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop := ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → f₁ x = f₂ x
274 
275 /-- `MapsTo f s t` means that the image of `s` is contained in `t`. -/
276 def MapsTo (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop := ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → f x ∈ t
277 
278 theorem mapsTo_image (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : MapsTo f s (f '' s) := fun _ ↦ mem_image_of_mem f
279 
280 theorem mapsTo_preimage (f : α → β) (t : Set β) : MapsTo f (f ⁻¹' t) t := fun _ ↦ id
281 
282 /-- Given a map `f` sending `s : Set α` into `t : Set β`, restrict domain of `f` to `s`
283 and the codomain to `t`. Same as `Subtype.map`. -/
284 def MapsTo.restrict (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) (h : MapsTo f s t) : s → t :=
285   Subtype.map f h
286 
287 /-- The restriction of a function onto the preimage of a set. -/
288 @[simps!]
289 def restrictPreimage (t : Set β) (f : α → β) : f ⁻¹' t → t :=
290   (Set.mapsTo_preimage f t).restrict _ _ _
291 
292 /-- `f` is injective on `s` if the restriction of `f` to `s` is injective. -/
293 def InjOn (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop :=
294   ∀ ⦃x₁ : α⦄, x₁ ∈ s → ∀ ⦃x₂ : α⦄, x₂ ∈ s → f x₁ = f x₂ → x₁ = x₂
295 
296 /-- The graph of a function `f : α → β` on a set `s`. -/
297 def graphOn (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Set (α × β) := (fun x ↦ (x, f x)) '' s
298 
299 /-- `f` is surjective from `s` to `t` if `t` is contained in the image of `s`. -/
300 def SurjOn (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop := t ⊆ f '' s
301 
302 /-- `f` is bijective from `s` to `t` if `f` is injective on `s` and `f '' s = t`. -/
303 def BijOn (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop := MapsTo f s t ∧ InjOn f s ∧ SurjOn f s t
304 
305 /-- `g` is a left inverse to `f` on `s` means that `g (f x) = x` for all `x ∈ s`. -/
306 def LeftInvOn (g : β → α) (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Prop := ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → g (f x) = x
307 
308 /-- `g` is a right inverse to `f` on `t` if `f (g x) = x` for all `x ∈ t`. -/
309 abbrev RightInvOn (g : β → α) (f : α → β) (t : Set β) : Prop := LeftInvOn f g t
310 
311 /-- `g` is an inverse to `f` viewed as a map from `s` to `t` -/
312 def InvOn (g : β → α) (f : α → β) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Prop :=
313   LeftInvOn g f s ∧ RightInvOn g f t
314 
315 section image2
316 
317 /-- The image of a binary function `f : α → β → γ` as a function `Set α → Set β → Set γ`.
318 Mathematically this should be thought of as the image of the corresponding function `α × β → γ`. -/
319 def image2 (f : α → β → γ) (s : Set α) (t : Set β) : Set γ := {c | ∃ a ∈ s, ∃ b ∈ t, f a b = c}
320 
321 variable {f : α → β → γ} {s : Set α} {t : Set β} {a : α} {b : β} {c : γ}
322 
323 @[simp, grind =] theorem mem_image2 : c ∈ image2 f s t ↔ ∃ a ∈ s, ∃ b ∈ t, f a b = c := .rfl
324 
325 theorem mem_image2_of_mem (ha : a ∈ s) (hb : b ∈ t) : f a b ∈ image2 f s t :=
326   ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
327 
328 end image2
329 
330 /-- Given a set `s` of functions `α → β` and `t : Set α`, `seq s t` is the union of `f '' t` over
331 all `f ∈ s`. -/
332 def seq (s : Set (α → β)) (t : Set α) : Set β := image2 (fun f ↦ f) s t
333 
334 @[simp, grind =]
335 theorem mem_seq_iff {s : Set (α → β)} {t : Set α} {b : β} :
336     b ∈ seq s t ↔ ∃ f ∈ s, ∃ a ∈ t, (f : α → β) a = b :=
337   Iff.rfl
338 
339 lemma seq_eq_image2 (s : Set (α → β)) (t : Set α) : seq s t = image2 (fun f a ↦ f a) s t := rfl
340 
341 end Set
